Notes: ROUND AN (Anthony: the match on the base's own pitch, seen diagonally like a drone shot). true = the match is drawn tilted onto match_ground.png; false = the flat pitch and the village of Stadium.csv, as before. The football itself is the same either way: only the drawing is tilted (src/core/pitch_view.gd).
The picture under the whole match: the base town, zoomed in (tools/make_match_ground.py, data/MatchGround.csv). Its top-left corner is at 0,0 and it is drawn at its own size.
The size of the pitch picture in Stadium.csv (soccerfield.png).
Where its white lines are inside that picture: x, y, width, height (tools/make_pitch.py prints these).
Where the TOP-LEFT corner of the white lines lands in match_ground.png (pixels). The base pitch's left corner. These three corners decide the tilt; the fourth follows.
Where the TOP-RIGHT corner lands: the base pitch's top corner.
Where the BOTTOM-LEFT corner lands: the base pitch's bottom corner. (The bottom-right corner then lands at about 2766,1065.)

How much of the town the wide shot shows round the tilted pitch, as a fraction of the pitch's own size on screen. 0 = the pitch just fits; 0.5 = a lot of town. The pushed-in shots (Tuning.csv camera_zoom, camera_zoom_close) are multiples of the pitch, as before.
The boards round the pitch (Anthony: like a German village club ground): the title screen's front-view boards strip, repeated and slanted along each edge.
How tall the boards stand, in picture pixels.
How far outside the white lines they stand, in match pixels.
